title: Pick a ripe strawberry off a potted plant without bruising it or tearing its stalk, and put it in a basket
instruction: Pick the strawberry and put it in the basket.
context: Picking strawberries is familiar from gardens and pick-your-own farms, and the hard part is physical. A berry pulled straight along its stalk needs 13.94 N to come off, but bent against it only 3.17 N (Dimeas et al. 2013); pulled straight, the stalk can also break midway and leave a piece that punctures other berries (Yamamoto et al. 2014). Gripped harder than about 10 N it bruises: a light grip slips, a hard one bruises, so the berry must be tilted before it is pulled.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the table top. Pot: a black plastic 6 in azalea pot (15.2 cm across the top, 11.4 cm at the bottom, 11.4 cm tall, soil 0.4 cm below the rim), centred at (38.0, -10.0). Plant: a day-neutral strawberry plant (e.g. 'Albion') with one ripe berry and no other ripe fruit; its leaves, flowers and any green fruit on the far half of the pot. The ripe berry's fruit truss (about 2 mm thick) rises from the crown among the leaf stalks to about 15 cm high, arches towards the robot over the near rim on the pot's centre line (y -10.0), about 1 cm above the rim, and hangs down beyond it, the berry's own stalk nearly straight down to the calyx. Berry: fully red, 14-16 g, about 2.8 cm across and 3.6 cm long, hanging tip down with its centre at (26.5, -10.0), 5.9 cm high, 3.5 cm beyond the rim (turn and place the pot so it does). Out of season, a long-stem strawberry (sold for chocolate dipping, stalk about 5 cm) stands in, its stalk joined to the end of a fruit truss with a 2.5 mm silicone grafting clip so the berry hangs at the same place. Basket: a square green molded-fiber quart berry basket (Pactiv 1 qt: 14.0 cm square at the top, 10.8 cm at the bottom, 8.3 cm tall), empty, centred at (23.0, -25.0). The left arm has nothing to do.
scoring: Tools: the trial video, a close-up photo of the berry taken right after the trial, and a ruler. Squeezed: at any moment a robot finger pressed the berry with more than 10 N (in simulation, the contact force; on real trials, a dented, flattened or leaking patch 3 mm or more across where a finger pressed); the trial then scores 0. Off: the berry no longer hangs from the plant. Torn: a piece of stalk more than 10 mm long remains above its calyx (in simulation, it came off with the pull within 45 degrees of its axis). In the basket: its centre inside the basket's walls and the berry resting on the basket's floor, any way up. Released: no part of the robot touches it. At the end: 0 if squeezed or still on the plant; 0.5 if off but not in the basket (held, on the table or on the floor), or if off and torn wherever it lies; 0.75 if off, not torn and in the basket but still touched; 1.0 if off, not torn, in the basket and released, held for 1 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: One berry is used per trial. Turn the pot so the truss of the plant's next ripe berry arches over the near rim and the berry hangs as in the setup (out of season, clip a fresh long-stem berry to a truss end), and empty the basket. Use berries that are fully red and firm.
fidelity: Berry: the YCB strawberry scan, 15 g, convex-hull collider, pad friction 0.5. Truss and stalk: 17 bending 1 cm links from the crown that droop under the berry. The berry hangs on a stiff spring and comes off when the pull reaches 13.94/(1+3.40 sin a) N, a being the pull's angle to its axis: the measured 13.94 N straight and 3.17 N tilted, with a smooth curve between. Torn below 45 degrees is a modelling choice. Leaves don't collide; pot and basket are fixed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps; the right arm moved about between the pot and the basket and never grasped the berry); demo: 1.0
